name: mastra-contextual-governance

scripts.build: bun --bun next build && bun run --filter '*' build
scripts.typecheck: next typegen && tsc --noEmit && bun run --filter '*' typecheck

//: The root manifest is the app's since #3: the Next.js app that was apps/web lives at the repo root, and the workspaces are the services still to fold plus packages/*. `--filter '*'` in `build` and `typecheck` matches the workspaces and never the root, so neither recurses. There is no `test` script: at the root `bun test` runs every group in the repo, and a script scoped to one of them would read as the whole suite. The app's group is `bun test ./app-test/`.

The app runs on Bun, not Node, since #4: `build` is `bun --bun next build`, and `dev` and `start` pass `--bun` in `scripts/next.ts`. The control plane in `lib/control-plane/` opens `governance.db` with `bun:sqlite`, which Node cannot load, and `next`'s bin is `#!/usr/bin/env node`, which plain `bun run` honours. Measured on #4: under Node the build fails collecting page data and the route answers 500.

`dev` and `start` go through `scripts/next.ts` so that PORT comes from the root `.env.local`, the way it does for the three Bun services from theirs. `next dev --port ${PORT:-3000}` did not: the shell expanded it before anything read the file, and the service bound 3000 in a worktree that owns 4410. See #50 and the comment at the top of that script; `app-test/dev-port.test.ts` fails if the shell-expanded form comes back. `dev:web` is the name the app ran under before #3, kept as an alias.

zod is pinned to one exact 4.x version, repo-wide, by the override below. The old 3.x pin (#28) guarded an Arcade TypeScript SDK this repo never depended on, and by #187 it blocked @mastra/mcp 2, whose MCP SDK requires zod ^4.2. One version everywhere is the point: two zods in one process disagree about instanceof.

apps/idp is a workspace member since #187: with the override at zod 4, Better Auth installs from the root like everything else, so a fresh clone needs one `bun install` and there is one lockfile. It is still the enterprise IdP stand-in a forker deletes, so it depends on nothing in the template and nothing depends on it — apps/idp/test/knows-people-not-loans.test.ts enforces both halves.

dev:idp-stub keeps `--cwd apps/loan-app` because that is where the stub lives, but it binds IDP_PUBLIC_HOST's port, not the PORT in that directory's .env.local — which is the loan API's. See #56 and the comment at the top of apps/loan-app/scripts/dev-idp.ts; apps/loan-app/test/dev-idp-port.test.ts fails if it goes back to PORT.

`studio` is `mastra dev`: it bundles `src/mastra/index.ts` and serves Mastra Studio under Node, on `STUDIO_PORT` rather than on `PORT`, which is the app's and which `mastra dev` would otherwise read from the root `.env.local`. Studio runs the chat route's agent and authorizes against the gateway itself, at `/arcade/authorize` on its own server (#8). In an Orca worktree `scripts/orca-setup.sh` sets `STUDIO_PORT` from the worktree's block; unset, Studio takes Mastra's own default, 4111, deliberately (`lib/agent/studio.ts::MASTRA_DEFAULT_PORT`). `app-test/studio-dev-server.test.ts` boots it on a port the OS hands out.
//ws: `ws` is a transitive runtime dependency, declared here on purpose. `@mastra/core` opens it at module scope (`import WebSocket from "ws"`), and Bun's isolated install links only a package's *declared* dependencies — so without this line `ws` exists only under `node_modules/.bun/@mastra+core@…/node_modules/ws` and is unreachable from the app. In the Alpine builder webpack left it as a bare `require("ws")` external, Next's file tracing could not resolve that specifier from the emitted route, and the standalone image shipped without it: `POST /api/chat` answered `Cannot find module 'ws'` on Render while `next start` on a full node_modules was fine. Declaring it is the whole fix — the specifier now resolves from this package, so tracing carries it. Measured in #92; `scripts/verify-standalone.ts` is what proves it, against the Docker image rather than `next start`.
//gc: `@cg/governance-core` is a runtime dependency since #4: the control plane is a module of this app (`lib/control-plane/`), and it is the engine's one consumer. The edge that matters runs the other way and still does not exist: `packages/governance-core` imports nothing from any app, and its `no-app-dependencies.test.ts` fails if it starts to. The UI side of the app still reaches the control plane only through its routes and `lib/control-plane/`'s exports, never the engine directly.
